backbone: Track a nonzero spherical class to its last nonzero suspension; show it is a square of a primitive annihilated root, exclude fourth powers; a Steenrod-module obstruction forces Hopf/Kervaire degrees.
quote: We show that this terminal class is a square \(z_e=w^2\) whose primitive, Steenrod-annihilated root still has nonzero suspension.

backbone: Transfer the model structure along the twice-extended Street nerve; the key nerve comparison for subdivided boundary/horn attachments is proved via stationary cylinders and induction on attached poset elements.
quote: Section~\ref{sec:transfer} supplies the model axioms, properness, and the unit comparison for arbitrary simplicial sets.

backbone: Construct a detecting map from L_K(3)S to a K(2)-local spectrum preserving a nonzero rational degree -3 stabilizer class; any splitting equivalence would kill it on pi_-3, a contradiction.
quote: Any equivalence \(X\simeq\mathcal W_3\) would force its lower horizontal map to vanish on \(\pi_{-3}\), and hence force the same for \(\tau_T\). This contradicts \cref{thm:main}.

backbone: Construct a glued connective spectrum via an operator with many pivot defects; defect growth N^beta beats an O(N^{1/3}) kernel bound, and backward induction excludes every finite tower from BP<2>.
quote: we construct a connective $p$-complete spectrum $X$ of exact fp-type two outside the ordinary thick subcategory generated by the specified standard form of $\BP\langle2\rangle_p^\wedge$.

backbone: Build two manifold models of one double cover via reflected cyclic covers; finite Out and a Sylow normalizer computation show a homeomorphism would force a forbidden conjugacy.
quote: We construct closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, disproving the homeomorphism-existence formulation of the Borel conjecture in dimension four.

backbone: Plus construction on an explicit five-generator presentation gives a D(2) complex with a torsion character of vanishing twisted H_2; a cyclic-cover tower obstruction shows no 2-complex has such a character.
quote: We construct a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex satisfying the $D(2)$ finiteness condition but not homotopy equivalent to any finite CW complex of dimension at most two.

backbone: Assume a positive maximal radial defect; attain it via ultrapowers, align extremal chords by a Darbo fixed point, and derive a contradiction from support and convexity estimates.
quote: We then align extremal chords using common supports and Darbo's fixed-point theorem and obtain a contradiction from support and convexity estimates.

backbone: Under CH, construct a coded dual space and perturbed predual with no separable quotient; under real-valued measurable c, a putative counterexample contradicts Hagler-Johnson; set-theoretic models give independence.
quote: For the negative implication, we build a dual space $E=X_0^*$ with coordinate vectors indexed by $\omega_1$.

backbone: Build X, Y as graph spaces over free spaces via a localized nonlinear Hilbert-space change of variables (finite stages, onto limit); complete continuity rules out linear isomorphism.
quote: There are separable real Banach spaces \(X,Y\) and a bijection \(\Psi:X\to Y\) such that, for every \(s,t\in X\),

backbone: Expand in exterior Faber polynomials, take singular vectors of P[A], and combine coefficient norm estimates into the bound 2; approximate general numerical ranges by smooth convex domains.
quote: We give a direct proof of the sharp constant-two numerical-range inequality for matrix-valued polynomials in all finite base and coefficient dimensions.

backbone: Prove uniform Walsh decay for finite-rank operators by an iterated halving inequality, transfer it to the identity via AP factorizations; uniform l_1^s copies are excluded, so K-convex.
quote: Uniform Walsh decay passes to \(J\), and then to every finite Walsh input in \(X\). Uniform copies of \(\ell_1^s\) would contradict that decay.

backbone: Assume X is not superreflexive; build an equal-sign-additive spreading norm, then finite reversible chart-chains whose labelled walks have linear displacement, contradicting Markov type p>1.
quote: We argue by contradiction. The James--Enflo characterization supplies a nonreflexive space finitely representable in a nonsuperreflexive one.

backbone: Assume a fixed-point-free map on a minimal invariant set; build an anchor via a semigroup idempotent and an inductive tree of maps with separating functionals; switching leaves contradicts.
quote: We argue by contradiction for the remainder of the proof and fix $K,T,Y$, and $(z_i)$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:reduction}.

backbone: Construct bodies from finite-field polynomial partition matrices with chosen parameters; uniform compression bounds the polar covering numbers while separated rows force large primal covering, violating duality.
quote: For every proposed pair of universal constants, we construct origin-symmetric convex bodies that violate the corresponding covering-entropy inequality, already when the covering body is a cube.

backbone: Glue bounded blocks built from colored regular graphs with label anchors; in each block, a norm-p finite-rank operator with small anchor error contradicts signed-measure tests.
quote: We construct a countable uniformly discrete space for which no such bound exists.

backbone: Define X as the dual of a segment-forest norm; verify reflexivity and no AUC renorming, prove a paired midpoint inequality, and sum quadratic midpoint losses over diamond levels for distortion.
quote: We construct a separable reflexive real Banach space whose given norm is asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex but which admits no asymptotically uniformly convex equivalent norm.

backbone: For given points and chain, define y_i via cut representation, a flat map with quartic potential and a stopped martingale, then bound energies to get Markov cotype two.
quote: The resulting points have a simple interpretation: each $y_i$ is the expected coordinatewise median of three independent geometric-walk endpoints started at $i$.

backbone: Starting from a scaled spherical immersion, add primitive metrics one at a time by oscillatory velocity loops, and correct exactly via an iterated smoothing scheme converging in every smooth norm.
quote: Smoothing between successive steps controls the lost derivatives; increasing the accuracy in successive blocks gives convergence in every smooth norm.

backbone: Place shrinking obstructed patches (generic metrics with no admissible height, via an oscillatory pulse estimate) around negatively curved disks accumulating at the origin; a boundary-saddle argument excludes any immersion.
quote: We construct a smooth positive-definite Riemannian metric on \((-1,1)^2\) that agrees with the Euclidean metric to every order at the origin, yet no neighborhood of the origin admits a smooth isometric immersion into Euclidean three-space.

backbone: Conformally reduce to scalar curvature -1; build a bounded-cohomology detector, iterate sweeps to entropy metrics, prove a measured degree estimate, and compare dual chains to bound simplicial volume.
quote: The work of this paper is the passage from that qualitative vanishing result to a uniform quantitative estimate.

backbone: Turn spectral positivity into a quadratic reserve by graph enlargement, run local stretching rounds with signed drift, and feed the data to the partition theorem.
quote: For an arbitrary complete metric $h$ and smooth $w$, we construct a smooth function $u$, a global graph metric $h^+=h+\dd u^2$, and a new signed drift $t^+$ such that

backbone: Minimize perimeter at fixed volume in large balls; a sharp hypersurface critical Sobolev inequality applied to the profile minimizers gives a differential inequality that integrates to the model comparison.
quote: This gives one differential inequality whose integral is exactly the model comparison.

backbone: Construct a global Kahler-Ricci flow, prove Harnack inequalities via a disc envelope, obtain contracting holomorphic charts, and iterate polynomial models so inverse charts converge to a biholomorphism onto C^n.
quote: Inverse iteration of these models makes the corrected inverse charts converge to an injective holomorphic map $M\to\C^n$.

backbone: Entropy equality gives a cohomological identity; contracting plaque jets, algebraic hulls and formal symmetries force smooth stable/unstable distributions, and classical smooth rigidity yields local symmetry.
quote: We prove that entropy equality forces precisely this missing smoothness. The proof has four stages.

backbone: From a kernel class in pi_9 of stable tubes, build a one-critical-point generating family and an exact embedded Lagrangian; Hamiltonian transport of a Morse family yields a contradiction.
quote: For some sufficiently large even integer $N$, we construct a closed exact smoothly embedded Lagrangian in $T^*(S^9\times S^{N-1})$ that is diffeomorphic to the base but is not Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section.

backbone: Use families Seiberg-Witten/Taubes curves over the coefficient sphere to build a nodal torus fibration, construct an auxiliary equal-square pair via nodal and regular-fiber models, and interpolate to a hyperkahler triple.
quote: construct the torus fibration, and \Cref{sec:local-models,sec:regular-preparation,sec:auxiliary-volume} construct the auxiliary equal-square pair. The proof of \Cref{thm:main} is completed in \Cref{sec:endpoint}.

backbone: If no compatible form exists, separation gives a positive current vanishing on closed invariant forms; mass-growth, angular and density estimates make it pair nonpositively with the taming form, a contradiction.
quote: In the argument below, separation gives a positive functional vanishing on closed invariant forms. An explicit elliptic lift and quantitative current estimates connect this obstruction to the existence of a taming form.

backbone: Split into three cases; in each, build Kahler/toric normal models from projective degenerations along curves cut out by quadrics, transfer symplectically, and pack via a surface packing lemma.
quote: We construct surface models of this shell in two stages: first a normal line over a hyperplane, then a normal model

backbone: Prove a sharp lower volume bound by Lagrangian Jacobi-field comparison and a model upper volume bound from topology (Pontryagin classes, signature); equality then forces isometry to the model CROSS.
quote: If a Blaschke manifold has volume at most that of its model at the same diameter, then it is isometric to that model.

backbone: Assume finitely many prime geodesic images; bound temporary sublevel classes by a uniform filling estimate via string-topology cut-join, then double-loop symmetry and equivariant classes give a contradiction.
quote: We first control these temporary classes and then use the symmetry of double loops to obtain a contradiction.

backbone: Assume dim Sing > s > m-1; find flat scales with many density-Q centers, blow up the height against fitted graphs via signed excess, and dimension-reduce limits to a contradiction.
quote: Suppose that $V$ is a stationary integral $m$-varifold in an open subset of $\R^{m+n}$ and that \[ m-1<s<\dim_{\Hh}\Sing(V). \]
